name: Vertex-level Pruning in Mixed-Primitive Gaussian Splatting
definition: A pruning mechanism that removes unnecessary vertices from mixed-primitive splats (Gaussian triangles and lines) during learning to refine the representation, in addition to standard primitive-level opacity pruning.
summary: Vertex-level pruning in Mixed-Primitive Gaussian Splatting removes redundant vertices to convert complex primitives into simpler shapes, reducing storage overhead while refining surface representation.
